children: and Swiss-based commodities trader Mercuria Energy are among firms interested in a deal for Venezuela's largest aluminium smelter, Bloomberg News reported on Friday.

The two companies are in separate discussions with the Venezuelan government about a deal for the Venalum smelter that could include operating the facility and gaining access to the aluminium it produces, according to people familiar with the matter.
Mercuria is working with private mining investment firm Heeney Capital on the potential deal, though no final agreement has been reached, the report said.

Venalum, also referred to as CVG Venezolana del Aluminio, is a state-owned Venezuelan aluminium producer that operates in Puerto Ordaz in Bolivar state, with capacity to roughly produce 430,000 metric tons of primary aluminium per year.
Glencore declined to comment on the report, while Mercuria Energy and Venalum did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.
Glencore had ties to Venezuela's aluminium industry more than two decades ago and later extended financing to the country's aluminium producers, according to the report.
Earlier this year, Glencore bought a 45% interest in an aluminium recycling and remelting plant near Charleston, South Carolina, expanding its footprint in the U.S. aluminium market.
Aluminium prices had climbed to a three-week high earlier this month, driven by supply tightness as a result of the Middle East tensions.
